message.content:
**Common proteins found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Protein (examples) | Typical function | |----------|--------------------|------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (sodium‑potassium pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)**
• **Aquaporin‑4**
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers)
• **Cadherins** (e.g., E‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Claudins** (tight‑junction strands)
• **Tetraspanins** (e.g., CD9, CD63) | Transport of ions, sugars, water; signal transduction; cell‑cell adhesion; intercellular communication | | **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane skeleton)
• **Actin‑binding proteins** – e.g., fimbrin, cofilin
• **Myosin‑1** (actin‑based motor)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger, peripheral to the cytoskeleton) | Structural support, anchoring integral proteins, cytoskeletal dynamics | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | • **GPI‑anchored proteins** – e.g., CD59, prion protein (PrP^C)
• **Palmitoylated proteins** – e.g., Src family kinases (c‑Src) | Signal transduction, membrane organization, cell‑surface recognition | These proteins together give the plasma membrane its selective permeability, signaling capabilities, and mechanical stability.
